text: A test only works as a governance gate if a failure actually stops something. This lesson explains why dbt build, not separate run and test commands, is the real production pattern.

Running dbt run then dbt test as two commands builds every model first, no matter what. dbt build interleaves tests into the dependency order itself, stopping before it ever builds on top of something that just failed.

Walk through a real failure: payments and the payment summary build fine, orders builds and then fails its non_negative test on amount, and customers — which depends on orders — never gets built that run at all.

This platform uses the default severity error, deliberately, not severity warn. A negative amount reaching lifetime value and then Power BI is a worse outcome than a build stopping and asking a human to look at it.

This gate becomes a real governance control only once it runs automatically on every proposed change — exactly what Chapter 6's CI pipeline wires up next, with no developer action required to trigger it.
